notes:
Inbound SMB from e-commerce personalization space. Signed up to Hosted API for trial — primary goal: power a support chatbot + product Q&A and summarization of order threads. Very cost sensitive: small margins, "need predictable hosting costs" stated by CTO Ramon Mendes. Current traffic: ~1k unique users/month, expect to double after Q2 campaign. Expected steady-state qps: 3-8 (peak ~20 qps), latency target: <500ms for 95th pctl on chat responses.

Key asks from discovery call:
- Token usage audit: customer wants a breakdown of where tokens are being spent (system vs user vs assistant) across sample prompts. Wants a CSV template to drop in their raw logs.
- Batching & caching recommendations: they run 70% of requests with small context windows (~300 tokens) and think batching could help reduce cost on background embedding/rerank jobs.
- Prompt compression / truncation guidance: asks for best practices to compress user prompts and keep useful context without hurting quality.
- Per-route cost attribution: need to show product/marketing teams the ROI per feature (support chat vs product search).

Security: request for SOC2 evidence and audit logging for hosted API. No immediate need for VPC/private but may ask later. Public cloud (AWS us-east-1) only.

Quotes & snippets: "If we can't get predictable sub-$3k/mo costs for chat at scale, hard to justify replacing current small ML infra." — R. Mendes, CTO.

Notes from AE/SE: SE (Liam) to assemble a small token-audit workbook + sample batching config. Offer short POC: run their last 72-hour traffic through Redwood's token-cost analyzer (anonymized) and return a one-pager with 3 concrete levers to save 30-50% (e.g., prefix caching, dynamic batching on background jobs, prompt templating).

Admin/ops: asked about rate limits, quotas, and whether we surface per-API-key token breakdowns in Console. They requested screenshots of Console cost views and the SDK quickstart. Linked drive doc contains the playbook shared: drive.google.com/drive/folders/1CostPlaybook-Silvercove
